deliberation: The regime is vulnerable to social impersonation, standing-policy authority laundering, confused-deputy inputs, sybil review, replay, revocation races, indirect control-plane effects, task decomposition, transitive workflows, excess credentials, and incomplete audit. The direction is not rejected because a closed low-risk execution class may be defensible, but only committee-built capabilities, schemas, hostile tests, and shadow evidence can make that claim reviewable.
discharged_obligations: Attacked impersonation, authority laundering, credentials, independence, replay, revocation, classification, composition, and audit completeness.
findings: Standing classes can launder instance-level reserved approval.
Control-plane effects can occur indirectly through dependencies and triggered systems.
Revocation and hold checks race queued or credentialed execution.
Distinct identities may share one controller and provide no separation.
Short-lived tokens may retain excess transitive capability.
Composition of small tasks can create prohibited aggregate effects.
amendments: Use single-task capabilities and atomic authorization consumption where possible.
Bind semantic dependency closure, generator, policy, base, output, credential, and exact target.
Protect classifiers and denied-capability policy from the proxy system.
Require unmistakable machine attribution and independent append-only audit.
Test confused deputy, replay, revocation, composition, symlink/submodule indirection, spoofed checks, and collusion.
residual_uncertainty: No implementation, permission matrix, identity model, or downstream consumer inventory exists.
